claims.text: The starting Al0.5CoCrFeNi alloy is single-phase and has a uniform room-temperature microstructure.
Simultaneous high-temperature DSC and dilatometry, combined with rigorous in-situ calibration, can accurately determine melting temperature in single-phase HEAs.
The combined method can accurately determine enthalpy of fusion in single-phase HEAs.
The combined method can accurately determine entropy of fusion in single-phase HEAs.
The combined method can accurately determine volume change during melting in single-phase HEAs.
Modulated heating and cooling at approximately 5–10 °C/min ensures thermal equilibrium during the measurements.
An inert atmosphere can be used for high-temperature thermal-analysis measurements while limiting contamination.
Gold and alumina melting or transition properties can serve as calibration references for high-temperature thermal analysis.
The cited calibration protocol establishes accurate calibration of both DSC and dilatometry.
The onset of melting is marked by a sharp endothermic DSC feature.
The onset of melting is accompanied by a sudden volume expansion in the dilatometry trace.
Fusion enthalpy can be obtained from the integrated thermal peak after sensitivity calibration.
Fusion entropy can be derived by integrating specific-heat variation.
Melting-induced volume-change data determine or inform liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The method will determine HEA melting temperatures within ±5 °C.
The method will determine latent heat of fusion within ±3–5%.
The method will provide quantitatively reliable fusion entropy and volume change across FCC, BCC, and HCP HEAs.
Separate DSC or dilatometry measurements are typically less accurate because of calibration drift and resolution limitations.
The approach is most applicable to well-characterized, single-phase HEAs with sharp melting transitions, whereas multiphase or inhomogeneous alloys require additional validation.
A melting-temperature error greater than ±5 °C, a latent-heat error greater than ±5%, or failure of DSC and dilatometry to agree within accepted uncertainty would falsify the proposed method.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator calls the DSC endotherm a latent-heat release, whereas an endothermic melting signal during heating represents heat absorption.

The intervention heats only to just above the solidus, but the hypothesis claims full fusion enthalpy, entropy, and melting volume change. For an alloy with a solidus–liquidus interval, just exceeding the solidus would not complete melting or capture the full fusion signal.
